pected weakness in VLMs. We analyze this weakness by                 as the primary metric. sMAPE is given by:
providing the model with additional clues and information.

5. Related Work                                                       6. Conclusion
                                                                      We introduced CAPTUR E, a novel benchmark for amodal
Spatial reasoning in visual question answering. Past                  counting that measures spatial reasoning capabilities under
work measures the spatial reasoning capabilities of VLMs              occlusion. CAPTUR E is designed to assess VLMs’ abil-
in the form of visual question answering (VQA) [4, 16]                ity to form a robust world model and use that model for
benchmarks. SpartQA [26] asks VLMs to identify the spa-               visual reasoning skills under occlusion. By testing count-
tial relation (e.g., above, behind, left of) between objects          ing, we cast the problem as a measurable task with an
in synthetically created 2D images from NLVR [39]. More               objective correct answer that also has real-world utility as
recent benchmarks test similar spatial relation understand-           VLMs become more broadly adopted. Our results suggest
ing with real images [2, 24, 36]. While this past work asks           that VLMs struggle to combine reasoning, counting, and
models to provide a text description for a relation between           world modeling with low performance on occluded and un-
two fully observed objects, CAPTUR E measures the world               occluded images. Our analysis indicates that models im-
modeling from a partially observed scene, thus requiring              prove with oracle information about visible objects (sim-
the handling of occlusion, pattern recognition, and count-            plifying the reasoning/counting tasks) and predicted infor-
ing. Together, these constitute a stricter test of spatial rea-       mation about the occluded objects (also simplifying world
soning than typical VQA settings.                                     modeling), pointing to directions of model improvement.
Amodal completion. Occlusions are common in natural

etc.) to finally dealing with fine-grained order perception           monsense (MCS) Grant N66001-19-2-4031, ARO Award
(multiple stacked occluded objects) [5]. Specifically in Qiu          W911NF2110220, ONR Grant N00014-23-1-2356, Mi-
and Di [34], VLMs classify the hidden objects and extract             crosoft Accelerate Foundation Models Research (AFMR)
fine details from occluded items. CAPTUR E, however,                  grant program, and a Bloomberg Data Science PhD Fellow-

cent error (MAPE) initially seems appealing but is dispro-                                                                             tern rigidity, we apply the following condition: ePyes ≥ T .

cluded split.

age. Assume the pattern of [dot shape]s continues
behind any black box. Provide the total number of
[dot shape]s as if the black box were not there. Only
count [dot shape]s that are visible within the frame (or
would be visible without the occluding box). If [dot
shape]s are partially in the frame (i.e. if any part of
[dot shape]s are visible), count it. If the [dot shape]s
would be partially in the frame without the occluding
box, count it.

TUR Esynthetic occluded split.

age. Assume the pattern of [dot shape]s continues

count [dot shape]s that are visible within the frame (or

shape]s are partially in the frame (i.e. if any part of
[dot shape]s are visible), count it. If the [dot shape]s
would be partially in the frame without the occluding
box, count it.
